llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its stated radar purpose, but contradictory documentation and small design choices (magic consent token in CLI, inconsistent requirements, and docs that show raw BPM fields despite promises to never expose them) make its privacy claims and operational assumptions unclear.

dimensions.detail: The code and instructions implement GPIO and UART interaction, FMCW/quantization semantics, and produce semantic vital-state outputs — these align with the stated mmWave radar purpose. However, the SKILL.md metadata requires python3/pyserial while the registry summary lists no required binaries (inconsistency). The agent docs also reference tapping raw ADC hardware (DCA1000EVM), which is plausible for an advanced radar use-case but raises deployment complexity that should be expected and verified.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions tell the agent to exec spectrum.py against device nodes (/dev/ttyUSB0) and include a literal consent token string. The code enforces that token value on the CLI, but the docs and examples are inconsistent about whether raw BPM numeric fields are ever exposed: spectrum.py returns only semantic labels (heart_status, breathing_status), yet S2-MEMZERO-PROTOCOL.md and AGENT-EXAMPLES.md show numeric bpm fields. This contradiction weakens the privacy guarantee and could lead an agent or integrator to log or store sensitive numeric vitals despite the 'never output exact BPM' claim.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No installer or remote downloads are included; the skill is instruction+script only. SKILL.md recommends installing standard system python libs (numpy, scipy) and pyserial via apt/pip — these are expected for local signal processing and serial I/O and pose normal, low install risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request external credentials or environment variables. However it relies on a CLI 'consent-token' argument whose example is a fixed literal (AUTH_S2_USER_GRANTED). Passing sensitive tokens on the command line can expose them via process listings or shell history. There are no network endpoints or external auths in the code, which is proportionate to the declared purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-included and does not request elevated agent privileges or system-wide config changes. The code claims to 'memzero' raw values and to avoid long-term storage; this is appropriate, but the documentation inconsistency about numeric BPM fields undermines trust that ephemerality is consistently enforced.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement local radar GPIO/UART parsing and returns quantized vital states, but there are a few red flags to resolve before installing: 1) Documentation inconsistency — the module code returns only semantic vitals, yet other docs show numeric BPM fields; ask the author to clarify and remove any examples that expose raw BPMs. 2) The CLI uses a hardcoded example consent token; avoid passing secrets on the command line (they appear in process lists and shell history). Prefer an authenticated flow or environment-based secret handling. 3) Confirm required system packages (python3, pyserial, numpy/scipy) before deployment; the registry metadata omitted these. 4) Review networking/logging on the host to ensure the agent or OS won't inadvertently persist sensitive telemetry (logs, monitoring agents, crash reports). 5) Because this code interacts with device nodes (/dev/ttyUSB0), test it in a controlled environment with dummy hardware first. If the author cannot reconcile the privacy documentation (memzero/quantization) with the examples and protocol docs, treat the privacy claims as unverified.
